# Basis as option: cases, model notes and G10 market differences

Detail behind steps 2-4 and 7 of [SKILL.md](../SKILL.md). Valuation engine: [fut-ctd-switch-and-delivery-options](../../fut-ctd-switch-and-delivery-options/SKILL.md).

## 1. Delivery-option model notes
- **One-factor model** (Huggins and Schaller, Fixed Income Relative Value Analysis, 2024, Ch.7): DO payoff is roughly a put or call (not exactly linear, because of convexity); strike is the inflection point; always out of the money, only time value, zero at delivery.
  Box 7.1: (1) map each deliverable's yield over a range of CTD yields at delivery with regression betas; (2) find inflection points; (3) decompose into puts and calls; (4) price each at the futures-option implied vol at a strike near the switch yield; (5) Black-Scholes and sum.
  Alternative: integrate the payoff over the CTD-yield density implied by futures options (better for markedly convex payoffs, not with large skew).
- Spread-vol input: historical spread vol of similar bonds is of limited use until they compete for CTD; scale pre-basket history by the average pre-delivery increase. DO is roughly linear in spread vol through the origin; correlations are stable and matter little. Multi-factor models push net bases up; market net bases are structurally too low far from the notional coupon.
- Illustrative one-factor run: parallel shifts, 40% lognormal yield vol, 10,000 simulations (Duering, Fixed Income Trading and Risk Management, 2021, Ch.28).
- Burghardt grid (The Treasury Bond Basis, 2005, Ch.4): build joint level x slope distribution (3x3 minimum); per cell identify CTD, value EOM option, `F = (CTD price - CTD carry - EOM option)/CTD CF`, compute each issue's BNOC; probability-weight. Steepening reduces BNOC when yields fall, flattening raises it, reversed when yields rise.
  Spread vol does not scale with root-time because yield changes are positively correlated. Yield betas are unstable and drive the model value; systematic flattening as yields rise reduces switch value; non-systematic spread vol (buybacks, squeezes, issuance) raises it.
- Early delivery: with negative carry and low vol the remaining option is below the negative carry, so the short delivers on day one and futures converge to CTD price / CF; with high vol the short waits. Expected futures = P(early) x E[CTD price/CF at early date] + P(late) x E[futures at last trading day].
- Wildcard recursion (JPM, Good things come to those who wait, 18 May 2018; `x ~ N(0, sigma^2)` post-close move, `C` = CF, `GB1` one day of gross basis): exercise on the eve of the last trade date iff `x > x1 = GB1/(1 - C)`; `E1 = (1 - C){sigma^2 p(x1) + (x1/2)[1 + erf(x1/(sigma sqrt2))]}`; `x_n = (E_(n-1) + GB1)/(1 - C)`.
  Negative GB gives `x1 < 0`: exercise slightly out of the money to avoid negative basis. May 2018 sensitivities: sigma 1.0 (FOMC x1), 1.0 (FOMC x2), 1.5 (FOMC x2), 2.0 (FOMC x2).
- Wildcard vendor induction (RiskVal, Future CTD Scenario Analysis, 2024): `V(T)=0` at last trade date, continue iff `X_t = dB(1 - 1/q) + (q - 1)V_3PM(t) + V_3PM(t+1) > 0`. The guide prints two variants of the `E` term (page 20 vs 23): verify before coding.
- Total option value = switch + timing + EOM + wildcard; option-adjusted NB = NB - total x CF (RiskVal example: switch 2 5/8 + EOM 9 ticks = 11 5/8 ticks).

## 2. Option-adjusted basis in practice
- Exh 7.5 (Burghardt, 23 Apr 1992, June futures 98-02, repo 3.80%, model yield vol 10.1% / price vol 9.0%): CTD 8-1/8% 8/15/19 actual basis 27.5, carry 23.7, theoretical option 3.9, theoretical basis 27.6, OAB -0.12. 10-3/8% 11/15/12-07: OAB +1.30. All under about 1 tick, treated as fair.
- Exh 7.6: OAB history May 1989 to May 1992 mostly within +/-5 ticks; deferred OAB fell below -10 ticks before year-end 1990 and 1991.
- Exh 4 (4 Apr 2001, June bond): OAB negative for every deliverable, -3.0 to -4.5/32. 5-3/8% 2/31: BNOC 97, TDOV 101.5, delivering it instead of the CTD would lose nearly 3 points.
- Dec-2001 10y stress (projected 20 Sep 2001): parallel +/-60bp keeps projected basis at expiry within 6/32; +60bp with 7s/10s steepening of 1.5 sd gives 17/32, a low-probability event because the curve usually steepens in a rally.
- Crossovers (Burghardt Ch.2, 5 Apr 2001): below 4.98% the 8-7/8% 8/17 is CTD, 4.98-6.13% the 7-5/8% 11/22, above 6.13% the 5-1/2% 8/28. 7-5/8% 11/22 behaves like a straddle: unchanged yields BNOC about 1.5/32; -60bp +7/32 for a long basis; +60bp +19.5/32.
- CTD-by-shift tables: USZ6 CTD -40bp 4.75% Nov-43; -10bp May-44/May-45/Nov-44; 0 5% May-45; +20 4.625% Nov-45; +50 1.375% Aug-50. WNZ6 4% Nov-52 from -40 to +10, 2.25% Feb-52 from +30 (prose says +20) (Barclays, 20 Aug 2026).
- DOV levels (JPM, Oct 2026): USZ6 about 18/32 and WNZ6 about 7/32 at start of October after rising from near zero once the 30y passed about 5.6%; USZ6 +20bp adds about 4/32; WNZ6 DOV peaks about 25bp above current yields; six USZ6 bonds above 10% CTD probability within +/-100bp.
- Switch-threshold reading: required spread change vs its 1y sd (Buxl: 5.4bp vs 3.2bp, or +23.7bp parallel; OAT: 1.6bp flattening vs 0.2bp sd; BTP: 1.2bp steepening vs 1.2bp sd) (JPM, 2 Oct 2026).
- Regression caution: a one-month fit `OAT DOV (c) = 14.50 x yield% - 56.14, R2 90%` is not a model; DOV is non-monotonic (JPM, 2 Oct 2026).

## 3. Trade-level examples (long basis)
- BofA (10 Apr 2025): buy TYM5 CTD basis 4.375% 1/31/32 vs CF-weighted TYM5 at gross -1, net 0; target 1 tick, flat base case, stop -4; nets cheapest at the peak of the liquidation after 2 April 2025 tariffs; TY and UXY nets 0 to -0.5, "buy nets on dips below 0".
- JPM (31 Jul 2026, USZ6): buy $100mn 4.625% Nov-44 vs sell 851 USZ6 (notional/100k x CF 0.851); GB 16/32, term repo 3.87% to 31 Dec 2026, net about 2/32. A long basis at about 15/32 net is not attractive when funding may tighten late in the month (JPM, 2 Oct 2026).
- MS (27 Aug 2026): long 5% May-45 vs short USZ6: GB 17.02 ticks, net 5.52 ticks at 3.95% term repo.
- JPM (6 Mar 2020): WNM0 net basis underpriced by roughly 4-8 ticks vs the wildcard value; rates had rallied 32-40bp and 3Mx10Y vol rose more than 20bp trough to peak: a stress dislocation. Weighted steepeners were stopped out by vol: stop on vol regime breaks.
- Exh 7.8 trades (three of six, average of all six +3.3 ticks net of costs): Mar 10-3/8 hedged with 2.0 Mar 96 puts + 0.63 Mar 92 puts +7.8 ticks; Mar 7-1/4 '16 vs 1.56 Mar 94 calls + 1.47 Mar 98 calls +6.4; Mar 8-1/8 '19 vs 2.76 Mar 104 calls -0.5 (Burghardt, 2005, Ch.7).
- Treasury futures 2026 delivery table (JPM, 12 Aug 2026, front/back): US BNOC 2.3/4.4, switch 4.6/14.8, implied repo 3.16/3.50; WN BNOC 2.0/1.6, switch 0.8/3.8; UXY BNOC 0.3/0.2, only wildcard; TY BNOC 0.0/0.4, back option about 4+/32 with WI as CTD; carry to optimal delivery TU 1.6, FV -0.3 (only negative), TY 2.3, UXY 2.2, US 5.5, WN 3.8 ticks. Roll before the first delivery day to avoid delivery.
- Futures DV01 for hedging: contract BPV is the factor-scaled CTD BPV (BPV/CF); across a switch the CF-adjusted DV01 jumps about 35-37% for Buxl vs about 7-8% for OAT/BTP (JPM, 2 Oct 2026); the probability-weighted BPV/CF is smooth (JPM, 29 Oct 2026: USZ6 rule-of-thumb BPV jumps 1382 to 1675 at the last switch).

## 4. Market differences (G10)
- **USD**: CBOT TU/FV/TY/TN/UXY/US/UB/WN; CF notional 6% (cut from 8% in 2000, raising CTD uncertainty). Wildcard live (3pm ET close, notice evening). WN more wildcard-exposed (low CF), US more CTD extension in sell-offs; local-curve drivers 15s20s for US, 25s30s for WN (Barclays, 20 Aug 2026). Board vs swaption (SOFR swaptions) is the main vol cross-check.
  Last trading day: TU/3Y/FV last business day; TY/TN/US/TWE/WN seven business days before (verify against the rulebook). Vol inputs seen (price vol): UB 12.9-13.9%, US 11.6-12.5%, TY ~6.1%, UXY ~7.3-7.7%, FV ~4.3%, TU ~1.9% (JPM, 28 Oct 2026). Treasury buybacks reduce switch risk. Term repo to Dec-26 delivery about 4.00% (BofA, 10 Jul 2025).
- **EUR**: Eurex Schatz/Bobl/Bund (6% notional), Buxl (4%), OAT and BTP (6% notional in the source). Small deliverable sets, fixed delivery day, higher squeeze/fail risk. Schatz/Bobl/Bund CTDs have minimal switch risk (net basis 0c / 1c / 3c); Buxl, OAT, BTP are non-dominant when yields rise and the OAT switched while 100bp+ below 6% via a curve twist. No Board-equivalent listed option vs swaption series in the sources: vol check is the swaption surface.
- **GBP**: Long Gilt (notional 4% per the contract spec). Gilts trade cheap on average; ex-dividend rules can remove a CTD mid-month (Burghardt, 2005, cross-chapter notes). No gilt basis-vs-vol data in the packs: use OAB with the swaption surface only.
- **JPY**: JGB futures (7 to 10.5y basket): one-factor DO 1 sen vs multi-factor 7 sen; spread vol rises sharply into delivery; short-net-basis holders fear delivery of the new CTD, sell it and buy back the old one, widening the spread without a yield-level move (JGB 212 1.5% vs JGB 213 1.4%, both June 2009) (Huggins and Schaller, 2024, Ch.7).
- **CAD** (CGB 10y, 6% notional), **CHF** (Eurex CONF, 1%), **AUD** (cash-settled vs basket-average yield, no delivery option, so no basis-vs-vol), **SEK** (single designated bond, no switch option), **NZD, NOK**: contract terms come from `fut_static`; no basis-vs-vol material in the sources. For cash-settled or single-bond contracts the skill reduces to swaption/futures-option vol RV in [vol-rates-options-rv](../../vol-rates-options-rv/SKILL.md).

## 5. Wildcard evidence
- BofA (10 Jul 2025): long $100mm 4.75% 11/15/53 vs short 734 WN (CF 0.7342), gross 5 ticks, net 4; after 3pm +1 point: deliver, lose `734 x 5 x $31.25 = $114,688`, sell the $26.6mm tail (`100mm x (1 - CF)`) a point higher `+$266,000`. Net profit about $151K; the exercise gives up the remaining net basis, so it pays only when the post-close move exceeds `GB x CF / (1 - CF)` (0.43pt here).
- Burghardt (2005, Ch.2-3): CF 1.3093 CTD, 6/32 basis: a 25.4/32 aftermarket drop is needed (19.4/32 below invoice); an inverted curve raises wildcard value, since early delivery forfeits no positive carry.
- JPM (18 May 2018): TUM8 ~0.75 tick, FVM8 ~0.5 tick; TUM8 gross basis -1 to -2 ticks with 1.375% Mar-20 CTD, late delivery optimal only if gross basis > about -0.75 tick; FVM8 optimal late for CTD bases down to -3.5 ticks. JPM (4 Dec 2019): WN about 3 ticks of net basis; mid-Nov 2019 wildcard explained most FV-to-WN net-basis variation and distorted implied and term repo by 10-30bp in TYZ9, UXYZ9, USZ9; WN implied repo drops into each delivery month with a 50-100bp gap to term repo from a few ticks of option value (annualisation).
- Early / mid / late delivery: early = within 3 business days of first delivery date, late = within 3 of last (JPM, 4 Dec 2019). Option-adjusted metrics beat raw IRR into the roll and delivery month because the IRR denominator is small and the optimal day unknown.

## 6. Scenario and market-structure notes (BofA, US Treasury futures primer, 10 Jul 2025)
- Long CTD basis as a straddle (USU5, CTD 11/43): +50bp CTD becomes 11/44 and the 11/43 basis goes to about 6 ticks (from 7); +100bp CTD becomes 8/50 and the 11/53 basis is worth 61 ticks; -50bp or more CTD becomes 2/41. Use a yield-shift and twist grid, then compare the long-basis payoff with a replicating futures option (or swaption package) and, if the basis is cheaper, buy it and sell the option.
- Futures price `= CTD forward / CF - total option value`; futures PV01 `= sum_i P(CTD_i) x forward PV01_i` over the scenario grid. Any other weighting `W` satisfies `B - W x F = (B - CF x F) + (CF - W) x F`: a non-CTD bond against futures is a curve trade vs the CTD plus the CF basis.
- Flat-6% thought experiment: below 6% the shortest-duration bond is CTD and above 6% the longest, so a parallel rally shortens futures and a sell-off lengthens them (an upward-sloping basket favours the longest, an inverted one the shortest).
- FVU5 basket: 8 bonds (11/30/2029 to 6/30/2030, plus the 7/31, 8/31 and 9/30/30 issues to come), first delivery 9/2/2025, last 10/3/2025; the CTD Nov-2029 had net basis -0.5 ticks and the highest IRR on GC repo. Net bases were near 0 in 2025 (wildcard up to 4-5 ticks on some contracts) versus 10+ ticks when yields were near 6%.
- Contract sizes that affect basis notionals: TU $200k face (double-sized), FV/TY/UXY $100k; tick values $7.8125 (TU, FV), $15.625 (TY, UXY), $31.25 (US, WN). Last trade is the last business day of the month for TU/FV and seven business days before it for the others; FV delivers only original-issue 5y notes.
- Futures versus cash trading: about $645bn/day in futures against about $460bn/day primary-dealer cash volume (2023), so futures liquidity matters for hedging the options leg.
- Positioning: asset managers are generally short the basis (long futures as a leverage substitute, favoured when the curve is inverted) and levered funds long, in similar size; asset managers carry basis risk through the whole holding period.
